examples.en: If you listen carefully to what the teacher says, the exam gets easier.

examples.ko: 친구가 조언해 줬는데 제대로 귀담아듣지 않았어요.
examples.en: My friend gave me advice, but I didn't really listen to it.

examples.ko: 제 이야기를 귀담아들어 줘서 정말 고마워요.
examples.en: Thank you so much for listening carefully to my story.

examples.ko: 발표 내용을 귀담아들은 사람이 많지 않았어요.
examples.en: Not many people listened closely to the content of the presentation.
You won't regret it if you take your parents' advice to heart.

examples.ko: 안내 방송을 귀담아듣고 있다가 내릴 역을 놓치지 않았어요.
examples.en: I listened carefully to the announcements, so I didn't miss my stop.

explain: '듣다'보다 집중해서 마음에 새기며 듣는다는 느낌이 있어요. 조언, 충고, 말씀 앞에 많이 쓰고 '귀담아듣지 않다'처럼 부정형으로도 자주 나와요. 'ㄷ' 불규칙이라서 '귀담아들어요, 귀담아들으세요'로 바뀌고, 비슷한 말로 '새겨듣다'가 있어요.
explain_en: It feels like listening with focus and taking the words to heart, more than plain '듣다'. It is often used with advice, warnings and respectful words, and the negative form '귀담아듣지 않다' is very common. It is a ㄷ-irregular verb, so it becomes '귀담아들어요' and '귀담아들으세요'. A similar word is '새겨듣다'.

examples.ko: 옆집 소리가 시끄러워서 귀마개를 끼고 잤어요.
examples.en: The neighbors were noisy, so I slept with earplugs in.
Did you pack the earplugs for swimming too?
In winter you really need warm earmuffs.

examples.ko: 귀마개 없이는 도서관에서도 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: Without earplugs I can't concentrate even in the library.
Sorry, could you lend me a pair of earplugs?

examples.ko: 이 귀마개는 부드러워서 오래 껴도 안 아파요.
examples.en: These earplugs are soft, so they don't hurt even if I wear them for a long time.

explain: 소음을 막는 것, 수영할 때 쓰는 것, 추위를 막는 것을 모두 '귀마개'라고 불러요. 그래서 어떤 귀마개인지는 문장 속 상황으로 알 수 있어요. 보통 '귀마개를 끼다, 귀마개를 하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: Earplugs for noise, for swimming, and earmuffs for the cold are all called '귀마개'. You tell which one is meant from the situation in the sentence. People usually say '귀마개를 끼다' or '귀마개를 하다'.

en: inside of an ear; inner ear

examples.ko: 귓속에 벌레가 들어간 것 같아서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: I felt like a bug had gotten into my ear, so I went to the hospital.
The inside of my ears hurts if I wear earphones for a long time.
I got out of the shower and water had gotten inside my ear.
The inside of my ear itches, so I'm looking for a cotton swab.
I wiped the inside of my ears clean after the bath.

examples.ko: 소리가 너무 커서 귓속까지 울리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: The sound is so loud it feels like it rings deep inside my ears.

explain: 일상에서는 '귓속' 단독보다 '귓속말'이 훨씬 많이 나와요. '귓속말로 말하다, 귓속말을 하다'는 남이 못 듣게 귀 가까이에 대고 작게 말한다는 뜻이고, '귀엣말'이라고도 해요. 발음은 사이시옷 때문에 [귀쏙]이에요.
explain_en: In daily life you will meet '귓속말' (a whisper) far more often than '귓속' alone. '귓속말로 말하다' means to speak quietly close to someone's ear so others can't hear; it is also called '귀엣말'. Because of the sai-siot, it is pronounced [귀쏙].

examples.en: I write down each day's schedule in my notebook.

examples.ko: 저는 그날그날 기분에 따라 옷을 골라요.
examples.en: I pick my clothes depending on my mood each day.

examples.ko: 오늘 할 일은 그날그날 끝내는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best to finish each day's tasks on that same day.
Vegetable prices at the market differ from day to day.

examples.ko: 그날그날 배운 단어를 복습하면 잊어버리지 않아요.
examples.en: If you review the words you learn each day, you won't forget them.

examples.ko: 그날그날 먹고 싶은 음식을 골라서 먹어요.
examples.en: I choose and eat whatever I feel like eating each day.

explain: '매일'은 날마다 반복된다는 느낌이고, '그날그날'은 그날의 사정이나 기분에 맞춰 하루하루 달라진다는 느낌이 있어요. 그래서 '달라요, 다르다'와 자주 같이 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '그때그때'도 있어요.
explain_en: '매일' stresses that something repeats every day, while '그날그날' means day by day, adjusting to that day's situation or mood. That is why it often appears with '달라요' (is different). A similar word is '그때그때' (depending on each moment).

examples.en: I'll head over there right after I hang up.
The road is jammed, so don't go that way.
All my friends decided to gather there.

examples.ko: 택시 기사님께 그리로 가 달라고 말했어요.
examples.en: I asked the taxi driver to go that way.

examples.ko: 어제 거기 갔다 왔는데 그리로 가는 버스가 자주 없어요.
examples.en: I went there yesterday, and buses that go that way aren't frequent.

examples.ko: 그리로 쭉 가시면 편의점이 보일 거예요.
examples.en: If you go straight that way, you'll see a convenience store.

explain: '이리로, 그리로, 저리로'가 한 세트인데, '그리로'는 듣는 사람 쪽이나 앞에서 이미 말한 곳을 가리켜요. '거기로'와 비슷하지만 방향을 말하는 느낌이 더 강해서 길을 알려 줄 때 자주 써요. 뒤에는 '가다, 오다, 모이다' 같은 이동 동사가 와요.
explain_en: '이리로, 그리로, 저리로' form a set, and '그리로' points to the listener's side or a place already mentioned. It is close to '거기로' but feels more about direction, so it is common when giving directions. It is followed by movement verbs such as '가다', '오다' and '모이다'.

examples.en: I sent a postcard to my family from my trip.

examples.ko: 박물관 기념품 가게에서 그림엽서를 몇 장 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a few postcards at the museum gift shop.
The postcard my friend sent arrived today.

examples.ko: 이 그림엽서는 제주도 풍경이 아주 예뻐요.
examples.en: The Jeju Island scenery on this postcard is very pretty.
I wrote a short greeting on the back of the postcard.

examples.ko: 책상 앞 벽에 그림엽서 두 장을 붙여 놓았어요.
examples.en: I stuck two postcards on the wall in front of my desk.

explain: 그냥 '엽서'라고 해도 돼요. '그림엽서'는 한쪽에 그림이나 사진이 있는 엽서를 말해요. 보통 '그림엽서를 쓰다, 보내다, 부치다'처럼 말하고, 세는 단위는 '장'이에요.
explain_en: You can simply say '엽서' too; '그림엽서' is one with a picture or photo on one side. It is usually '그림엽서를 쓰다, 보내다, 부치다', and the counter is '장'.

examples.en: My car got scratched on a wall while parking, and I'm upset.
My arm got scratched while I was petting the cat.

examples.ko: 휴대폰 화면이 긁히지 않게 필름을 붙였어요.
examples.en: I put a film on my phone so the screen won't get scratched.

examples.ko: 가방 앞이 긁힌 걸 이제 봤어요.
examples.en: I only just noticed that the front of my bag is scratched.
Glass scratches easily, so wipe it carefully.
When the toe of my shoe gets scratched, I rub it with shoe polish.

explain: '긁다'의 피동 표현으로, 날카롭거나 거친 것에 스쳐서 표면에 자국이 나거나 살짝 상처가 나는 느낌이에요. 깊게 다치면 '베이다'를 쓰고, 살짝 스치면 '긁히다'를 써요. '자동차, 휴대폰, 피부'처럼 물건이나 몸에 모두 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is the passive of '긁다' and means a surface gets marked or lightly injured by something sharp or rough rubbing against it. For a deeper cut you say '베이다', and for a light scrape you say '긁히다'. It works for both objects (cars, phones) and skin.

examples.ko: 요즘 금값이 너무 올라서 반지 사기 부담돼요.
examples.en: Gold prices have risen so much that buying a ring is a burden.
The price of gold changes a little every day.

examples.ko: 금값도 한 번 오르면 쉽게 안 내려요.
examples.en: Once the price of gold goes up, it doesn't come down easily.
The news said gold prices hit a record high.

examples.ko: 금값 때문에 결혼반지 가격도 많이 올랐어요.
examples.en: Because of the price of gold, wedding ring prices went up a lot too.
I checked the gold price yesterday and it had gone up again.

explain: '금값이 오르다, 내리다, 떨어지다'처럼 가격이 움직이는 동사와 같이 써요. 금 가격 이야기라서 뉴스와 금은방 이야기에 자주 나와요. 발음은 사이시옷 때문에 [금깝]이에요.

phrases.en: Apples are crazy expensive these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 귀해지거나 값이 많이 올랐을 때 과장해서 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An exaggerated way to say something has become scarce or has shot up in price.

explain_en: It goes with verbs of price movement like '금값이 오르다, 내리다, 떨어지다'. Since it is about the price of gold, it shows up often in the news and at jewelry shops. Because of the sai-siot, it is pronounced [금깝].

examples.en: I read a story about someone finding a lump of gold in the mountains.
I didn't know a lump of gold was this heavy.
I took a photo in front of a huge lump of gold.
What would you do if you found a gold lump on the street?
I wish I could at least find a lump of gold.

examples.ko: 금덩어리처럼 노란 달이 산 위에 떴어요.
examples.en: A moon as yellow as a lump of gold rose above the mountain.

explain: 가공하기 전의 금이 덩어리로 있는 모습을 말할 때 써요. 금반지나 금시계처럼 만든 물건에는 쓰지 않아요. 줄여서 '금덩이'라고도 하며, 이야기나 동화에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It describes raw gold in a lump, before it is made into anything. It is not used for made items like gold rings or watches. It can be shortened to '금덩이', and it appears often in stories and fairy tales.

examples.en: My grandfather gave me a gold watch as a gift.
I want a gold watch as a graduation present.
My father used to wear this gold watch.
I went to the wedding wearing a gold watch on my wrist.
Even a gold watch gets a worn strap if you wear it for long.

examples.ko: 금시계 한 개 값이 얼마인지 아세요?
examples.en: Do you know how much a single gold watch costs?

explain: 시계는 손목에 '차다'라고 해서 '금시계를 차다'가 자연스러워요. 색만 금색인 시계는 '금색 시계'라고 하고, '금시계'는 금으로 만든 시계를 말해요. 비싼 물건이라서 선물이나 어른 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A watch is worn with the verb '차다', so '금시계를 차다' is the natural phrase. A watch that is only gold in color is a '금색 시계', while '금시계' is made of gold. It is expensive, so it often comes up in talk about gifts and elders.

examples.ko: 급행열차를 타면 서울까지 한 시간 걸려요.
examples.en: If you take the express train, it takes an hour to Seoul.
The express train doesn't stop at small stations.

examples.ko: 급행열차가 오기 전에 표를 사야 해요.
examples.en: We have to buy tickets before the express train arrives.

examples.ko: 급행열차 대신 완행열차를 타고 천천히 갔어요.
examples.en: I took a slow train instead of the express and went leisurely.
There were almost no seats on the express train.
To transfer to the express train, get off at the next station.

explain: 반대말은 모든 역에 서는 '완행열차'예요. 말할 때는 그냥 '급행'이라고 줄여서 말하는 경우도 많고, 지하철에도 '급행'이 있어요. 빠른 대신 서는 역이 적어서 어느 역에 서는지 꼭 확인해야 해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '완행열차', which stops at every station. In speech people often shorten it to '급행', and subways have a '급행' too. It is faster but stops at fewer stations, so check which stations it stops at.

examples.ko: 기내식으로 소고기와 생선 중에 고를 수 있어요.
examples.en: For the in-flight meal, you can choose between beef and fish.
I ate the in-flight meal on the plane and fell asleep right away.
I was surprised that the in-flight meal was tastier than I expected.
Special in-flight meals must be requested in advance.
I also requested a vegetarian in-flight meal.

examples.ko: 짧은 비행에서는 기내식 대신 간식만 줘요.
examples.en: On short flights they only give snacks instead of a meal.

explain: '기내'는 비행기 안이라는 뜻이라서 '기내식'은 비행기에서 주는 식사예요. '기내식을 먹다, 기내식이 나오다'처럼 쓰고, 비행기 안에서 파는 간식이나 음료는 보통 '기내식'이라고 하지 않아요.
explain_en: '기내' means inside the plane, so '기내식' is the meal served on a flight. You say '기내식을 먹다' or '기내식이 나오다'. Snacks or drinks sold on board are not usually called '기내식'.

examples.en: A monument stands in the middle of the square.
I took photos with friends in front of the monument.

examples.ko: 이 기념탑은 오래전 일을 기억하려고 세웠어요.
examples.en: This monument was built to remember something from long ago.
There's also a small monument at the entrance of the village.
I went early in the morning to see the monument.
The area around the monument is neatly kept.

explain: 어떤 일이나 사람을 기억하려고 탑 모양으로 높이 세운 것을 말해요. 비슷한 '기념비'는 비석 모양이라서 모양이 달라요. '기념탑을 세우다, 기념탑이 서 있다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is a tall structure shaped like a tower, built to remember an event or person. The similar '기념비' is a stone-tablet type, so the shape differs. You say '기념탑을 세우다' or '기념탑이 서 있다'.

examples.en: My grandmother reads a prayer every morning.

examples.ko: 이 기도문은 외우는 데 일주일 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took me a week to memorize this prayer.
Even a short prayer stays in your heart for a long time.

examples.ko: 기도문 몇 줄을 수첩에 적어 두었어요.
examples.en: I wrote down a few lines of a prayer in my notebook.

examples.ko: 친구가 기도문이 적힌 카드를 보내 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend sent me a card with a prayer written on it.

examples.ko: 여행 전에 가족이 함께 기도문을 소리 내어 읽었어요.
examples.en: Before the trip, our family read a prayer aloud together.

explain: '기도'는 마음속으로 빌거나 하는 행동이고, '기도문'은 글로 쓰인 기도의 내용이에요. 그래서 '기도문을 읽다, 외우다, 쓰다'처럼 글을 다루는 동사와 같이 써요. 종교에 따라 정해진 기도문이 있어요.
explain_en: '기도' is the act of praying, while '기도문' is the written text of a prayer. So it pairs with verbs for handling text, such as '기도문을 읽다, 외우다, 쓰다'. Many religions have set prayers.

examples.ko: 다음 달부터 택시 기본요금이 또 올라요.
examples.en: From next month, the basic taxi fare goes up again.

examples.ko: 기본요금만 내면 오 킬로미터까지 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you only pay the basic fare, you can go up to five kilometers.
Data is included in the phone's basic charge.
The distance was short, so it came to only the basic fare.
I first asked how much the basic charge was.

examples.ko: 기본요금 이후에는 거리에 따라 요금이 더 붙어요.
examples.en: After the basic charge, more is added depending on distance.

explain: 택시, 휴대폰, 주차장처럼 처음에 내야 하는 최소 요금을 말해요. 그 뒤에 이용한 만큼 더 내는 것은 '추가 요금'이라고 해요. '기본료'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is the minimum fee you pay at the start for things like taxis, phone plans and parking. What you pay on top of that, depending on use, is called '추가 요금'. People also say '기본료'.

en: might as well; if you're going to anyway

examples.en: If possible, please book a bigger room.

examples.ko: 배우는 김에 기왕이면 제대로 배우고 싶어요.
examples.en: Since I'm learning anyway, I want to learn it properly.

examples.ko: 기왕이면 같이 먹으면 더 좋지 않을까요?
examples.en: Wouldn't it be nicer to eat together, if we're going to anyway?
As for the gift, pick something practical if you can.
Take photos in a bright place if you can.

examples.ko: 기왕이면 이번 주말에 다 끝내 버려요.
examples.en: Since we're at it, let's finish it all this weekend.

explain: 같은 일을 할 거라면 더 좋은 쪽을 고르자는 마음으로 써요. '이왕이면'과 같은 뜻이고 둘 다 자주 말해요. 부탁이나 권유하는 문장 앞에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: You use it when you mean: if you are going to do it anyway, choose the better option. It means the same as '이왕이면', and people say both. It fits well at the start of requests and suggestions.

examples.en: The children are playing train in the yard.

examples.ko: 기차놀이 할 때는 앞사람 어깨를 꼭 잡아요.
examples.en: When playing train, you hold the shoulders of the person in front firmly.
My son says train play is the most fun.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 친구들과 기차놀이를 하며 뛰어다녔어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I ran around playing train with my friends.

examples.ko: 기차놀이를 하려고 아이들이 한 줄로 섰어요.
examples.en: The children lined up in a row to play train.
We line up in a row and walk like a train.

explain: 맨 앞 아이가 기관차, 뒤의 아이들이 객차가 되어 앞사람 어깨를 잡고 줄지어 움직여요. '술래잡기'와 달리 이기고 지는 게 없고, 유치원이나 마당에서 많이 해요. '기차놀이를 하다'로 써요.
explain_en: The first child is the engine and the others are the cars, holding the shoulders of the person in front as they move in a line. Unlike tag ('술래잡기'), nobody wins or loses, and it is common in kindergartens and yards. You say '기차놀이를 하다'.

examples.en: Only married people, please answer this survey.
The views of married and unmarried people were quite different.
Married people are also eligible to apply.

examples.ko: 회사 서류에 기혼자인지 적는 칸이 있어요.
examples.en: The company form has a box for whether you are married.
There are quite a lot of married people on our team.
A parenting class is held for married people.

explain: 반대말은 '미혼자'예요. 설문, 서류, 통계처럼 딱딱한 글에서 많이 쓰고, 대화에서 사람에게 직접 묻을 때는 '결혼하셨어요?'라고 해요. 사람 무리를 나눌 때 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '미혼자'. It is mostly used in formal writing such as surveys, forms and statistics, while in conversation you ask a person directly with '결혼하셨어요?'. It is a word for sorting groups of people.

examples.en: If you turn the street corner, my house is right there.
A small bakery opened on that street corner.
We decided to meet at that street corner tomorrow.

examples.ko: 길모퉁이 가게 아주머니가 항상 인사해 주세요.
examples.en: The lady at the corner shop always greets me.

examples.ko: 길모퉁이 쪽에서 갑자기 자전거가 나와서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: A bicycle suddenly came out from the corner and startled me.
Shall we walk slowly as far as the corner?

explain: 길이 꺾이거나 만나는 바깥쪽 모서리 부분을 말해요. 그냥 '모퉁이'라고도 하고, 좁은 길인 '골목'과는 달라요. '모퉁이를 돌다'처럼 이동하는 동사와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is the outer corner where a street bends or meets another. People also just say '모퉁이', and it is different from '골목', a narrow alley. It pairs well with movement verbs, as in '모퉁이를 돌다'.

examples.ko: 어제 김칫국을 끓였는데 아이가 잘 먹었어요.
examples.en: I made kimchi soup yesterday and my child ate it well.
I ate rice in cool, refreshing kimchi soup.

examples.ko: 김칫국이 너무 짜서 물을 더 넣었어요.
examples.en: The kimchi soup was too salty, so I added more water.
For breakfast I had a simple meal with leftover kimchi soup.
One bowl of kimchi soup settles my stomach.
In summer, kimchi soup is refreshing even when eaten cold.

explain: '김칫국'은 김치로 끓인 국이고, 김치에서 나온 국물 자체는 '김칫국물'이라고 해요. 옷에 묻는 건 대개 '김칫국물'이에요. 발음은 사이시옷 때문에 [김칟꾹]이에요.

phrases.example: 아직 결과도 안 나왔는데 김칫국부터 마시지 마세요.
phrases.en: Don't celebrate yet, the results haven't even come out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 줄 생각도 없는데 미리 기대하고 행동하는 사람을 놀리듯 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said teasingly about someone who expects something in advance before it is even decided.
phrases.en_equiv: count your chickens before they hatch

explain_en: '김칫국' is soup made with kimchi, while the liquid that comes out of kimchi itself is '김칫국물'. What stains clothes is usually '김칫국물'. Because of the sai-siot, it is pronounced [김칟꾹].

examples.en: The light in my room keeps flickering, which makes me uneasy.
Don't cross when the green light starts blinking.
I was so sleepy that my eyes kept blinking.
The stars are twinkling and flickering in the night sky.
I saw the phone's light blinking.
I changed the settings so the screen doesn't flicker.

explain: '깜박이다'보다 되풀이되는 느낌이 강해서 고장 난 전등이나 점멸 신호등에 잘 어울려요. '전등이 깜박거리다'처럼 주어에 '이/가'를 써요. 헷갈리기 쉬운 '깜박하다'는 '잊다'에 가까운 전혀 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It feels more repeated than '깜박이다', so it suits a faulty lamp or a blinking signal. You say '전등이 깜박거리다', with '이/가' on the subject. Don't confuse it with '깜박하다', a different word closer to 'forget'.

examples.en: The baby looked at me, blinking.
The car ahead went slowly with its hazard lights blinking.
A small light is flickering far away.
Every time I blinked, sleepiness washed over me.
I looked for a long time at the night sky with twinkling stars.

examples.ko: 눈에 먼지가 들어가서 눈을 자꾸 깜박였어요.
examples.en: Dust got in my eye, so I kept blinking.

explain: '깜박거리다'와 비슷하지만 '눈을 깜박이다'처럼 목적어를 받아 쓸 수 있어요. 운전할 때 방향지시등을 '깜빡이'라고도 말해요. '깜빡이다'로도 쓰는 같은 말이에요.
explain_en: It is similar to '깜박거리다' but can take an object, as in '눈을 깜박이다'. When driving, people also call the turn signal '깜빡이'. '깜빡이다' is another spelling of the same word.

examples.en: I accidentally broke a cup while washing dishes.
The child almost broke the window with a ball.
If you're not careful, you'll break the plate.

examples.ko: 그 말이 조용한 분위기를 깨트리고 말았어요.
examples.en: Those words ended up breaking the quiet atmosphere.

examples.ko: 친구와 한 약속을 깨트리면 신뢰를 잃어요.
examples.en: If you break a promise to a friend, you lose trust.
Please crack the egg and put it in the frying pan.

explain: '깨뜨리다'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰이는 표준어예요. 스스로 깨지는 '깨지다'와 달리 누가 일부러나 실수로 깨는 일에 써요. 컵뿐 아니라 약속, 기록, 분위기를 깨는 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It is a standard word with the same meaning as '깨뜨리다'. Unlike '깨지다' (to break by itself), it is for someone breaking something on purpose or by accident. Besides cups, it is used figuratively for promises, records and moods.

examples.en: I grilled and ate saury for dinner tonight.
I made tasty kimchi stew with canned saury.
I heard autumn saury tastes the best.

examples.ko: 꽁치는 뼈가 많아서 조심해서 먹어야 해요.
examples.en: Saury has many bones, so you have to eat it carefully.
I bought three saury at the market.
I served the grilled saury with grated radish.

explain: 몸이 길고 가늘어서 고등어와 모양이 달라요. 생선구이로도 먹지만 '꽁치 통조림'으로 찌개를 끓여 먹는 일도 많아요. 생선은 '한 마리, 두 마리'로 세요.
explain_en: It has a long, slim body, so it looks different from mackerel. It is eaten grilled, but many people also make stew with canned saury ('꽁치 통조림'). Fish are counted as '한 마리, 두 마리'.

examples.en: I planted a few flowering trees in the yard.
When spring comes, every flowering tree blooms.

examples.ko: 이 꽃나무는 물을 자주 줘야 해요.
examples.en: This flowering tree needs to be watered often.
We ate lunch boxes under a pretty flowering tree.
Flowering trees stand in a row along the road.

examples.ko: 꽃나무에 물을 주다가 벌에 쏘일 뻔했어요.
examples.en: I almost got stung by a bee while watering the flowering tree.

explain: 꽃이 피는 나무를 통틀어 말하는 쉬운 말이에요. 벚나무나 매화나무처럼 이름을 알면 이름으로 말하고, 이름을 모를 때 '꽃나무'라고 하면 편해요. 나무는 '한 그루, 두 그루'로 세요.
explain_en: It is an easy, general word for trees that bear flowers. If you know the name, like cherry or plum tree, you use that name, and '꽃나무' is handy when you don't. Trees are counted as '한 그루, 두 그루'.

en: meaning of a flower; language of flowers

examples.ko: 혹시 이 장미의 꽃말이 뭔지 아세요?
examples.en: Do you happen to know what this rose's flower meaning is?

examples.ko: 꽃을 고를 때 꽃말도 같이 봐요.
examples.en: When I choose flowers, I look at their meanings too.

examples.ko: 꽃말은 꽃 이름과 함께 외우면 쉬워요.
examples.en: Flower meanings are easy to remember along with the flower names.
I looked up the flower meanings and chose a birthday bouquet.

examples.ko: 꽃말 때문에 이 꽃은 선물하기 조심스러워요.
examples.en: Because of its flower meaning, I'm careful about giving this flower as a gift.

examples.ko: 꽃말에 대해 이야기하다가 이 가게를 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: I found this shop while talking about flower meanings.

explain: 꽃마다 따로 정해진 상징적인 뜻을 말해요. '꽃말이 뭐예요?', '꽃말이 사랑이에요'처럼 말하고, 선물할 꽃을 고를 때 자주 이야기해요. 발음은 [꼰말]이에요.
explain_en: It is the symbolic meaning assigned to each flower. You say things like '꽃말이 뭐예요?' or '꽃말이 사랑이에요', and it comes up often when choosing flowers as gifts. It is pronounced [꼰말].

examples.en: On Parents' Day, I sent my parents a flower basket.

examples.ko: 꽃바구니는 꽃병이 없어도 바로 둘 수 있어요.
examples.en: A flower basket can be set down right away without a vase.

examples.ko: 선생님 책상 위에 꽃바구니가 놓여 있었어요.
examples.en: A flower basket was sitting on the teacher's desk.
I also put a congratulations card in the flower basket.
Until what time is flower basket delivery available?
Flower baskets are pretty too, but I like bouquets.

explain: 바구니에 꽃을 꽂아 만든 선물이에요. 손에 묶어 드는 '꽃다발'과는 모양이 달라요. 개업, 어버이날, 축하 자리에서 '꽃바구니를 주문하다, 보내다'라고 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is a gift made by arranging flowers in a basket. It differs from a '꽃다발', which is a hand-held bunch tied together. You often hear '꽃바구니를 주문하다, 보내다' for openings, Parents' Day and celebrations.

examples.en: When the wind blew, cherry blossoms fell like rain.

examples.ko: 꽃비를 맞으며 공원을 한 바퀴 걸었어요.
examples.en: I walked once around the park in the petal rain.
The spring road with falling petals is really pretty.
Do you want to go to the riverside this weekend to see the falling petals?

examples.ko: 꽃비는 오래 볼 수 없어서 더 아쉬워요.
examples.en: You can't see the falling petals for long, which makes it more regrettable.
I walked slowly along the road covered with petals.

explain: 진짜 비가 아니라 꽃잎이 바람에 날려 비처럼 떨어지는 모습을 말해요. 주로 벚꽃이 질 때 봄에 많이 말해요. '꽃비가 내리다, 꽃비를 맞다'처럼 비 표현을 그대로 써요.
explain_en: It is not real rain but petals blown by the wind and falling like rain. It is most often said in spring when cherry blossoms drop. It uses ordinary rain expressions, as in '꽃비가 내리다' and '꽃비를 맞다'.

examples.en: The rose blossoms in the garden are in full bloom.

examples.ko: 꽃송이 하나를 꺾어서 책 사이에 끼웠어요.
examples.en: I picked one blossom and tucked it between the pages of a book.
A sunflower blossom is as big as a face.

examples.ko: 꽃송이마다 벌이 한 마리씩 앉아 있어요.
examples.en: A bee is sitting on each blossom.

examples.ko: 꽃송이를 몇 개만 골라 화병에 꽂았어요.
examples.en: I picked just a few blossoms and put them in a vase.
Big snowflakes are pouring down like blossoms outside the window.

explain: 줄기에 달린 꽃 한 덩이를 말해요. '꽃 한 송이'처럼 세는 단위 '송이'가 붙은 말이에요. '꽃'은 식물 전체를 가리킬 때도 있지만 '꽃송이'는 달려 있는 꽃의 덩어리를 말해요.
explain_en: It means one bloom on a stem, built on the counter '송이' as in '꽃 한 송이'. '꽃' can refer to the plant in general, but '꽃송이' points to the flower head itself.

examples.en: In spring I scattered flower seeds in the yard.
My friend gave me a packet of flower seeds.
The flower seeds are so small that they're easy to lose.
In autumn I collected seeds from wilted flowers.
I'm waiting for sprouts to come up from the flower seeds.

examples.ko: 꽃씨 심기 체험에 아이와 함께 갔어요.
examples.en: I went with my child to a flower seed planting activity.

explain: 꽃을 피우는 씨앗이에요. '꽃씨를 뿌리다, 심다, 받다'처럼 쓰고, '씨'만 말해도 되지만 '꽃씨'라고 하면 꽃이라는 걸 바로 알 수 있어요. 채소나 곡식 씨앗은 보통 '씨앗'이나 '씨'라고 해요.
explain_en: These are seeds that grow into flowers. You say '꽃씨를 뿌리다, 심다, 받다', and while '씨' alone works, '꽃씨' makes clear it's a flower. For vegetable or grain seeds, people usually say '씨앗' or '씨'.

en: floral scent; fragrance of a flower

examples.en: When I opened the window, the first thing I noticed was the scent of flowers.
Smelling flower fragrance makes me feel good.
The scent of flowers also comes carried on the spring breeze.
This scented candle has a gentle floral scent, which I like.
I was lost in the flower fragrance and stood there for a long time.

examples.ko: 꽃향기 때문에 재채기가 나는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people sneeze because of the scent of flowers.

explain: '냄새'보다 기분 좋은 느낌의 '향기'를 쓴 말이에요. '꽃향기를 맡다'처럼 '맡다'와 같이 써요. 가볍게는 '꽃냄새'라고도 하지만 좋은 향을 말할 때는 '꽃향기'가 더 어울려요.
explain_en: It uses '향기' (fragrance) rather than '냄새' (smell), so it has a pleasant feel. It pairs with '맡다', as in '꽃향기를 맡다'. People casually say '꽃냄새' too, but '꽃향기' suits a nice scent better.

examples.ko: 연락 없이 결근한 탓에 팀장님께 꾸중을 들었어요.
examples.en: I was scolded by my team leader for being absent without notice.

examples.ko: 숙제를 안 한 탓에 선생님께 꾸중을 들었어요.
examples.en: I got scolded by my teacher because I didn't do my homework.
The parents didn't scold the child harshly.

examples.ko: 선생님은 화를 내지 않고 조용히 꾸중하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher scolded quietly without getting angry.

examples.ko: 무조건 꾸중해도 소용없으니 먼저 이유를 물어봐요.
examples.en: Scolding without thinking is useless, so ask the reason first.

examples.ko: 꾸중을 들은 뒤에 동생이 방에서 울었어요.
examples.en: After being scolded, my younger sibling cried in the room.

explain: '혼내다'와 비슷하지만 더 딱딱하고, 보통 윗사람이 아랫사람의 잘못을 말로 나무랄 때 써요. 실제 대화에서는 '꾸중하다'보다 '꾸중을 듣다'로 많이 말하고, 편한 말로는 '혼나다'가 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '꾸짖다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is like '혼내다' but stiffer, usually used when someone senior scolds a junior about a mistake. In real conversation people more often say '꾸중을 듣다' (get scolded) than '꾸중하다', and the casual word is '혼나다'. A similar word is '꾸짖다'.

examples.en: Water after exercise tastes like heaven.

examples.ko: 소문난 식당이라 그런지 음식이 그야말로 꿀맛이었어요.
examples.en: Maybe because it's a famous restaurant, the food was absolutely delicious.

examples.ko: 배고플 때 먹는 라면은 정말 꿀맛이죠?
examples.en: Ramen when you're hungry is really delicious, right?
Lunch after working feels so good.
The watermelon is sweet, so it tastes amazing.
On a tiring day, a nap feels like pure bliss.

explain: 실제 꿀 맛보다는 '아주 맛있다'는 칭찬으로 많이 써요. 배고플 때나 힘든 일을 한 뒤에 먹는 음식에 잘 어울려요. 잠에는 비슷하게 '꿀잠'이라는 말을 써요.
explain_en: It is used far more as praise meaning 'really delicious' than for actual honey. It suits food eaten when you are hungry or after hard work. For sleep, there is the similar word '꿀잠'.

examples.ko: 감기 기운이 있어서 따뜻한 꿀물을 마셨어요.
examples.en: I felt a cold coming on, so I drank warm honey water.

examples.ko: 어머니가 꿀물 한 잔을 타 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother made me a cup of honey water.

examples.ko: 꿀물에 레몬을 조금 넣으면 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: If you add a little lemon to honey water, it tastes better.

examples.ko: 꿀물이 너무 달아서 물을 더 탔어요.
examples.en: The honey water was too sweet, so I added more water.
People drink honey water both hot and cold.
I soothed my stomach with warm honey water in the morning.

explain: 꿀을 물에 탄 음료예요. 가루나 액체를 물에 섞을 때는 '타다'를 써서 '꿀물을 타다'라고 말해요. 따뜻하게도 차갑게도 마시는 집에서 만드는 음료예요.
explain_en: It is a drink of honey mixed into water. When mixing powder or liquid into water you use '타다', so you say '꿀물을 타다'. It is a simple homemade drink served warm or cold.

examples.ko: 아이가 누운 지 오 분 만에 꿈나라였어요.
examples.en: The child was in dreamland within five minutes of lying down.

examples.ko: 동생은 지금 꿈나라에서 놀고 있나 봐요.
examples.en: My younger sibling must be off in dreamland now.
I brush my teeth before going off to dreamland.

examples.ko: 그림책 속 꿈나라 이야기를 읽어 줬어요.
examples.en: I read a story about dreamland from a picture book.
I should head to dreamland early today.

examples.ko: 꿈나라로 가는 기차가 나오는 동화를 좋아해요.
examples.en: I like fairy tales with a train to dreamland.

explain: 잠자는 동안 가는 상상의 세계를 말해서, 아이들 이야기나 잠자리 인사에 자주 나와요. 어른도 '벌써 꿈나라예요'처럼 장난스럽게 쓰기도 해요. 진지한 글보다 부드럽고 귀여운 말투에 어울려요.

phrases.example: 피곤했는지 저녁도 안 먹고 꿈나라로 갔어요.
phrases.en: He must have been tired, because he went off to sleep without eating dinner.
phrases.nuance_en: A cute, soft way of saying someone falls asleep.

explain_en: It is an imaginary world you go to while asleep, so it often appears in children's stories and bedtime talk. Adults also use it playfully, as in '벌써 꿈나라예요'. It suits a soft, cute tone more than serious writing.

examples.en: I have to finish the report today.
I finished class and went straight home.

examples.ko: 일을 끝마친 뒤에 같이 밥 먹어요.
examples.en: Let's eat together after finishing work.
I'm relieved that I got through the presentation safely.
I haven't been able to finish all my homework yet.

examples.ko: 공사를 끝마칠 때까지 한 달쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes about a month until the construction is finished.

explain: '끝내다, 마치다'와 비슷한데, 하던 일을 끝까지 해서 마무리한다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 일, 숙제, 수업, 발표처럼 해야 할 일을 목적어로 받아요. 일상 대화에서는 '끝내다'나 '마치다'가 더 편하게 들려요.
explain_en: It is like '끝내다' and '마치다', but with a stronger sense of seeing a task through to completion. It takes things you have to do as the object, such as work, homework, class and presentations. In daily conversation, '끝내다' or '마치다' sounds more casual.

examples.en: I played the word chain game with my family in the car.

examples.ko: 끝말잇기 하다가 생각이 안 나서 졌어요.
examples.en: I couldn't think of a word during the word chain game, so I lost.

examples.ko: 끝말잇기가 한국어 단어 공부에 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: The word chain game helps with studying Korean words.
I killed boredom with the kids by playing the word chain game.

examples.ko: 끝말잇기에서 이기려면 단어를 많이 알아야 해요.
examples.en: To win at the word chain game, you need to know a lot of words.

examples.ko: 끝말잇기는 앞사람이 말한 단어의 마지막 글자로 시작해요.
examples.en: In the word chain game, you start with the last letter of the previous person's word.

explain: 앞사람이 말한 단어의 마지막 글자로 시작하는 단어를 차례로 말하는 말놀이예요. 친구나 가족과 이동하는 시간에 심심할 때 자주 해요. '끝말잇기를 하다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is a word game in which each person says a word starting with the last syllable of the previous person's word. People often play it with friends or family when bored, such as during trips. You say '끝말잇기를 하다'.

examples.ko: 차선을 바꿀 때 끼어들기를 하면 위험해요.
examples.en: Cutting in when changing lanes is dangerous.
A sudden cut-in nearly made me hit the car ahead.

examples.ko: 줄을 설 때 끼어들기는 예의가 아니에요.
examples.en: Cutting in when waiting in line is bad manners.
It's a road with a lot of cutting in, so I drove slowly.
It was a no-cutting-in zone, so I just drove past.

examples.ko: 운전할 때는 끼어들기에도 신호를 꼭 켜야 해요.
examples.en: When driving, you must also use your signal when cutting in.

explain: 동사 '끼어들다'에서 나온 말로, 운전 중 차선에 끼어드는 것과 줄에 끼어드는 것에 모두 써요. 줄 서기에서 순서를 어기고 앞에 서는 것은 '새치기'라고도 하고, 둘 다 좋지 않게 보는 행동이에요. 운전 이야기에서는 도로 표지판에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It comes from the verb '끼어들다' and covers both cutting into a lane while driving and cutting into a line. Breaking the order in a queue is also called '새치기', and both are seen as rude. In driving contexts it often appears on road signs.
